details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) released its "World Economic Outlook, October 2026," projecting global growth to slow to 3.1% in 2026 and rebound to 3.4% in 2027. Global headline inflation is notably projected to rise to 4.7% in 2026 before easing to 4.1% in 2027. The IMF warns that major economies need "urgent" fiscal fixes due to elevated primary deficits and rising sovereign yields, emphasizing the growing divide between economies benefiting from the AI-driven investment boom and those facing higher import bills and weaker demand. Risks are skewed to the downside, with further escalation in conflicts and fiscal vulnerabilities potentially weakening growth.
title: Global Growth Slowdown & Rising Inflation Projected by IMF

details: US household inflation expectations have risen in October, according to the University of Michigan's final October survey. Year-ahead inflation expectations increased to 4.7% and long-run expectations to 3.5%, both reaching their highest readings since May. This data comes just ahead of the Federal Reserve's October 27-28 meeting. Consumer prices also rose hotter than expected, with the Consumer Price Index (CPI) increasing by 3.7% in the 12 months through September 2026, and the Producer Price Index (PPI) jumping 1.3% in September. Hot inflation raises the odds of continued hawkish monetary policy and potential interest rate hikes, which could negatively impact risk assets. The Fed is widely expected to hold rates at their upcoming meeting, but the focus will be on any signals regarding future rate adjustments, particularly for December.
title: US Inflation Expectations Rise Ahead of Federal Reserve Meeting

details: Bitcoin experienced a weekend selloff, briefly falling below the $80,000 mark and hitting $79,973. It is currently down 3.3% for October and 8.34% year-to-date. This downturn is attributed to several factors, including broader macroeconomic concerns such as rising inflation and the anticipation of potential Federal Reserve actions. Adding to the pressure, US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded a significant net outflow of $635.5 million on October 22, the largest single-day outflow since June, suggesting weakening institutional buying. Geopolitical tensions, particularly concerns about potential attacks by Iran and rising oil prices (Brent crude above $117), are also contributing to a risk-off sentiment in global markets, impacting Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies. Companies holding Bitcoin on their balance sheets have an average cost of around $80,000 per coin, making this a critical support level.
title: Bitcoin Dips Below $80,000 Amid ETF Outflows and Geopolitical Tensions
